skills.name: Component Filter Logic
skills.tool: Client-side filter utility (JavaScript, operates on incidents array from GET /api/incidents)

testcases.name: returns full list when component filter is 'all'

skills.capability: Implement a pure function that filters the incident list to only those affecting a selected component, returning the full unfiltered list when no component (or 'all') is selected.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing the component-filtering logic for the incident dashboard timeline/list. Write a pure, side-effect-free function that takes the full incidents array and a component value, and returns only incidents whose `component` field matches; when the value is 'all' or falsy, return the full list unchanged so clearing the filter restores everything. Do not mutate the input array.
acceptance_criteria: filterByComponent(incidents, 'API') returns only incidents where component === 'API'
filterByComponent(incidents, 'all') returns the full, unfiltered incident list

skills.name: Component Filter Dropdown UI
skills.tool: React component (select/dropdown) bound to incident list state
skills.capability: Build a dropdown/select control populated with the unique set of affected components from the incident data, wired to SKILL_001's filter function, with a default 'All Components' option that clears the filter.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the component-filter dropdown that sits above the incident timeline/list. Derive the list of selectable components from the unique `component` values present in the incidents array (deduplicated, sorted), include an 'All Components' option first, and on selection call the existing filterByComponent utility to update the visible list; selecting 'All Components' must restore the full incident list exactly as it was before any filter was applied.
acceptance_criteria: getUniqueComponents(incidents) returns a deduplicated, sorted array of component names present in the data
Selecting a component in the dropdown updates the rendered incident list to only that component's incidents
Selecting 'All Components' (or clearing the filter) restores the full incident list with no residual filtering

skills.name: Severity Filter Logic
skills.tool: Client-side filter utility (JavaScript, operates on incidents array from GET /api/incidents)

testcases.name: returns full list when severity filter is 'all'

skills.capability: Implement a pure function that filters the incident list by severity level (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3), returning the full list when severity is unset or 'all'.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing severity-based filtering for the incident dashboard timeline/list. Write a pure function that takes the incidents array and a severity value (e.g. 'SEV1', 'SEV2', 'SEV3', or 'all'), and returns only incidents whose `severity` field matches; when severity is 'all' or falsy, return the full unfiltered list. Do not mutate the input array or introduce severity color logic here — that belongs to the existing State Chips component.
acceptance_criteria: filterBySeverity(incidents, 'SEV1') returns only incidents where severity === 'SEV1'
filterBySeverity(incidents, 'all') returns the full, unfiltered incident list

skills.name: Severity Filter Control UI
skills.tool: React component (toggle/chip group) bound to incident list state, reusing State Chips styling tokens
skills.capability: Build a severity filter control (button group or chip toggles reusing the existing State Chips design tokens) that applies SKILL_003's filter function and supports clearing back to all severities.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the severity filter control above the incident timeline/list. Reuse the existing State Chips component's severity color tokens (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) so filter chips visually match the chips already shown on incidents, and never introduce new colors for this control. Wire selection/deselection to the filterBySeverity utility, and ensure deselecting all severities (or an explicit 'All' toggle) restores the full incident list.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a severity chip updates the rendered incident list to only that severity's incidents
Clearing the severity filter restores the full incident list
Severity filter chips use only the existing State Chips color tokens, with zero new colors introduced

skills.name: Date Range Filter Logic
skills.tool: Client-side filter utility (JavaScript, operates on incidents array from GET /api/incidents)

testcases.name: filters incidents within inclusive date range
returns full list when no date range is set

skills.capability: Implement a pure function that filters the incident list to those whose timestamp falls within an inclusive start/end date range, returning the full list when no range is set.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing date-range filtering for the incident dashboard timeline/list. Write a pure function that takes the incidents array plus a startDate and endDate (ISO strings or null), and returns only incidents whose `createdAt` timestamp falls within the inclusive range; when both startDate and endDate are null/undefined, return the full unfiltered list. Handle partial ranges (only startDate or only endDate provided).
acceptance_criteria: filterByDateRange(incidents, startDate, endDate) returns only incidents with createdAt within the inclusive [startDate, endDate] range
filterByDateRange(incidents, null, null) returns the full, unfiltered incident list

skills.name: Date Range Picker UI
skills.tool: React component (date range picker) bound to incident list state
skills.capability: Build a date range picker control above the incident timeline/list that applies SKILL_005's filter function and supports clearing the range to restore the full list.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the date range picker for the incident dashboard timeline/list. Provide start and end date inputs, wire changes to the filterByDateRange utility to update the visible incidents, and include a 'Clear' action that resets both dates to null so the full incident list is restored. Validate that startDate is not after endDate before applying the filter.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a start and end date updates the rendered incident list to only incidents within that range
Clearing the date range restores the full incident list
An invalid range (startDate after endDate) does not apply a broken filter

skills.name: Combined Filter State & Clear All

testcases.name: applies component and severity filters together
clearFilters default state returns full list when applied

skills.capability: Implement a combined filter function that applies component, severity, and date-range filters together (AND logic) against the incident list, plus a reset helper that restores the full list when all filters are cleared.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing the combined filter state for the incident dashboard timeline/list, which lets component, severity, and date-range filters be applied simultaneously. Write applyFilters(incidents, filters) that composes filterByComponent, filterBySeverity, and filterByDateRange with AND semantics, and a clearFilters() helper returning the default filter state ({component: 'all', severity: 'all', startDate: null, endDate: null}) such that applying it returns the full incident list unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: applyFilters(incidents, {component, severity, startDate, endDate}) returns only incidents matching all active filter criteria simultaneously
applyFilters(incidents, clearFilters()) returns the full, unfiltered incident list
